summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn closed the Build My Church series with a message titled Go After the One. Pastor Travis reminded Impact Church that the church is not being built simply to have a church. It is being built for people who are not here yet: the lost, the hurting, the weary, and anyone who believes God could never love them. Looking back on the early years of the church, he said his answer to how big the church should be has always been "one more."

Drawing from Luke 15 and Luke 19:10, he showed that Jesus actively seeks and saves the lost, leaving the ninety-nine to pursue the one. He connected this to the Great Commandment and the Great Commission, teaching that the gospel was never meant to be kept private and that believers are not only people who attend church but the church that goes. He challenged listeners to consider what their daily lives communicate about Jesus, since people often form opinions about Christ long before they ever visit a service.

Three points shaped the message. First, found people find people. In Matthew 4, Jesus called fishermen to follow him and promised to send them out, changing what they would spend their lives pursuing. Those who have been found were likely reached by someone who prayed, invited, or shared. Second, if I don't go, how will they know? Using Romans 10:13-15, Pastor Travis urged believers to stop being passive, reminding them that someone must speak, invite, and tell others that Jesus loves them and that no one is too far gone. He shared the account of a Sunday school teacher who obeyed a nudge to share Jesus with a teenage shoe salesman named Dwight Moody, and he pointed to Andrew bringing his brother Simon to Jesus in John 1. Third, you don't need a sermon, you need a story. Pointing to the man healed of blindness in John 9, he encouraged everyone to simply tell what Jesus has done for them, since a changed life is a powerful testimony (Revelation 12:11).

The service ended with an invitation for anyone who wanted to surrender their life to Jesus. Many raised their hands, and Pastor Travis led the congregation in a prayer of repentance and new life. Erica then encouraged the online campus to pray for their one and invite them to Bring a Friend Sunday next week, and to give faithfully so more people can encounter Jesus.
mainPoints: Found people find people: those who have been found by Jesus are changed in what they pursue and are sent to reach others.
If I don't go, how will they know? Someone must speak, invite, and share the good news, and that someone is you.
You don't need a sermon, you need a story: simply telling what Jesus has done in your life is a powerful testimony.

versesMentioned.text: Suppose one of you has a hundred sheep and loses one of them. Doesn't he leave the ninety-nine in the open country and go after the lost sheep until he finds it?
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.

Jesus replied: "'Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.' This is the first and greatest commandment. And the second is like it: 'Love your neighbor as yourself.'"
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
For I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God that brings salvation to everyone who believes: first to the Jew, then to the Gentile.
If anyone is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will be ashamed of them when he comes in his Father's glory with the holy angels.
Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own;
Since my people are crushed, I am crushed; I mourn, and horror grips me.
But if I say, "I will not mention his word or speak anymore in his name," his word is in my heart like a fire, a fire shut up in my bones. I am weary of holding it in; indeed, I cannot.

As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the lake, for they were fishermen. "Come, follow me," Jesus said, "and I will send you out to fish for people." At once they left their nets and followed him. Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, preparing their nets. Jesus called them, and immediately they left the boat and their father and followed him.

for, "Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved." How, then, can they call on the one they have not believed in? And how can they believe in the one of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone preaching to them? And how can anyone preach unless they are sent? As it is written: "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!"

The first thing Andrew did was to find his brother Simon and tell him, "We have found the Messiah" (that is, the Christ). And he brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, "You are Simon son of John. You will be called Cephas" (which means Peter).
Those who accepted his message were baptized, and about three thousand were added to their number that day.
He replied, "Whether he is a sinner or not, I don't know. One thing I do know. I was blind but now I see!"
Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!
They triumphed over him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony; they did not love their lives so much as to shrink from death.

Monday.scripture: Luke 19:10 (NIV): "For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost."
Monday.focus: Identify your one. Jesus actively seeks people, and he invites us to share his heart for them.
Monday.action: Write down the name of one person God has placed on your heart. Keep it somewhere you will see it each day this week.
Monday.prayer: Jesus, thank you for seeking me when I was lost. Give me your heart for the person I wrote down today. Open my eyes to see them the way you do. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Romans 10:14 (NIV): "And how can they believe in the one of whom they have not heard?"
Tuesday.focus: Be willing to go. Someone has to speak up, and God may be sending you.
Tuesday.action: Send a kind, encouraging text or note to your one today, simply letting them know you are thinking of them and praying for them.
Tuesday.prayer: Lord, make my feet willing to go. Give me courage to reach out and kindness to show your love in a simple way today. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: John 9:25 (NIV): "One thing I do know. I was blind but now I see!"
Wednesday.focus: Remember your story. You do not need a sermon, only an honest account of what Jesus has done for you.
Wednesday.action: Write three or four sentences about your life before Jesus, how you met him, and how he has changed you.
Wednesday.prayer: Father, thank you for the story you are writing in my life. Help me remember what you have done and give me the words to share it humbly and clearly. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Matthew 4:19 (NIV): "Come, follow me," Jesus said, "and I will send you out to fish for people."
Thursday.focus: Following Jesus changes what we pursue. Ask God to shift your priorities toward people.
Thursday.action: Look for one natural opportunity today to ask someone, "How can I pray for you?" and then pray for them, even briefly.
Thursday.prayer: Jesus, change what I am fishing for. Help me care more about people than about my own comfort and plans. Send me where you want me to go. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Romans 1:16 (NIV): "For I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God that brings salvation to everyone who believes."
Friday.focus: Courage over silence. The good news is too good to keep private.
Friday.action: Share a short version of your story with someone, or invite your one to join you for Bring a Friend Sunday, in person or online.
Friday.prayer: God, take away any fear or shame that keeps me quiet. Give me boldness and gentleness as I share the hope I have in you. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: John 1:41-42 (NIV): "The first thing Andrew did was to find his brother Simon and tell him, 'We have found the Messiah.' And he brought him to Jesus."
Saturday.focus: Prepare to bring someone with you. One simple invitation can open a door God has already been working on.
Saturday.action: Confirm your invitation for tomorrow. Invite your one to church, or send them the online service link and offer to watch together. Then pray for them by name.
Saturday.prayer: Lord, prepare the heart of the person I am inviting. Let tomorrow be a day of encounter with you, and help me trust you with the results. Amen.

title: How to Share Your Faith Without Fear | Go After the One
